options: An asset that has already been fully depreciated
An asset that has been retired
An asset still being built or assembled, accumulating cost but not yet depreciating
An asset that exists only in a tax book
questions.explain: A CIP asset tracks accumulated cost for something still under construction or assembly, but it does not depreciate while in CIP status.

questions.q: Why doesn't a CIP asset depreciate while under construction, no matter how much cost has accumulated?
options: Because CIP assets are not allowed to have any cost
Because it isn't yet producing any economic benefit
Because CIP assets are automatically retired after 90 days
Because depreciation methods don't apply to machinery
questions.explain: Depreciation reflects consumption of economic benefit; an asset not yet in use isn't producing that benefit, so recognizing depreciation wouldn't be meaningful.

questions.q: What two things happen when a CIP asset is capitalized?
options: It is deleted and a new asset is created from scratch
It is merged into a different asset category automatically
Its accumulated cost is written off as an expense
Its status converts to a regular depreciable asset, and a date placed in service is set
questions.explain: Capitalizing converts the CIP asset to a regular depreciable asset and establishes the date placed in service that starts the depreciation clock.

questions.q: In the paint booth example, why does depreciation not apply to the invoices received in January and February?
options: Because those invoices were miscoded
Because January and February fall in a closed period
Because the category assigned no salvage value
Because the asset was capitalized April 1, and depreciation starts from the date placed in service, not the invoice dates
questions.explain: Depreciation starts from the date placed in service (April 1 in this example), regardless of when the individual costs were originally invoiced during construction.

questions.q: What financial reporting problem does holding depreciation until capitalization prevent?
options: Understating the asset's cost
Causing the asset to be assigned to the wrong book
Overstating depreciation expense during construction and understating it once the asset is actually productive
Preventing the asset from ever being retired
questions.explain: If CIP assets depreciated during construction, expense would be recognized before the asset generates any benefit, mismatching expense recognition with actual use.
